claims.text: Texas Tech and Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists are developing AI tools for irrigation decisions.
claims.quote:
a team
                           of Texas Tech and Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists are developing artificial
                           intelligence-driven tools to help farmers make more precise irrigation decisions.
claims.scope_note: Development effort, not a deployed irrigation controller or tested result.

claims.text: Researchers plan crop field trials under different irrigation conditions.
claims.quote:
Researchers say the sites will allow them to develop, test and refine the multi-scale
                           phenotyping framework under real-world conditions. Each location is equipped with
                           subsurface irrigation systems that enable precise control of water applications, creating
                           a range of irrigation scenarios that simulate varying degrees of crop water stress.
claims.scope_note: Planned trials; comparing conditions is a plain-language description of the stated range of irrigation scenarios.

claims.text: Subsurface irrigation systems at the trial sites enable control of water applications.
claims.quote:
Each location is equipped with
                           subsurface irrigation systems that enable precise control of water applications, creating
                           a range of irrigation scenarios that simulate varying degrees of crop water stress.
claims.scope_note: Buried lines are a generic illustration of subsurface irrigation. No source evidence of individual nozzle control, autonomous pivot control or an algorithm controlling water.

claims.text: The planned framework collects crop water stress data from drones, ground sensors and satellite imagery.
claims.quote:
The research team aims to create a standardized framework capable of collecting and
                           analyzing crop water stress data from multiple sources, including unmanned aircraft
                           systems, ground-based sensors and satellite imagery.
claims.scope_note: Planned sensing workflow. Do not invent sensing wavelengths, accuracy, specific sensors or measured crop response.

claims.text: The project aims to combine crop water stress observations in a centralized database.
claims.quote:
The project’s objectives include developing a centralized database for multi-scale
                           crop water stress data
claims.scope_note: Objective, not evidence that the database is complete or operating.

claims.text: The project aims to use machine learning to predict crop growth under different irrigation conditions.
claims.quote:
creating machine learning models that can predict crop growth
                           and development under different irrigation conditions
claims.scope_note: Planned model capability, not a validated prediction or implemented irrigation algorithm.

claims.text: The goal is irrigation recommendations for growers.
claims.quote:
Artificial intelligence will
                           then be used to transform that information into practical recommendations for irrigation
                           management.
claims.scope_note: Proposed recommendations, not automated actuation, deployed advisory service or proven outcome.

claims.text: Planned trial sites include a commercial farm near Slaton, Texas.
claims.quote:
Field trials for the project will be conducted at three locations: a Texas Tech research
                           field, a Texas A&M AgriLife research field and a commercial farm near Slaton, Texas.
claims.scope_note: Planned trial location. Generic plot is not the actual Slaton farm, and no commercial farm result is reported.

claims.text: Improved water-use efficiency is an anticipated benefit of the project.
claims.quote:
Anticipated benefits include improved water-use efficiency, greater crop resilience
                           and a scalable model for precision water management in water-limited agricultural
                           regions.
claims.scope_note: Water savings are a goal. This announcement supplies no measured savings, yields or completed validation results.

claims.quote:
The project, titled "Developing a Multi-Scale Phenotyping Framework Integrating Machine
                           Learning for Crop Water Stress Assessment," is led by Wenxuan Guo, associate professor
                           of crop ecophysiology and precision agriculture at Texas Tech and Texas A&M AgriLife
                           Research.
claims.scope_note: Named research lead. No depiction of a real person may be inferred from a generic illustration.

rejected.claim: Completed field trials or proven irrigation recommendations
rejected.reason: The source describes planned trials, objectives and anticipated benefits, not completed testing or validated model performance.

rejected.claim: Measured water savings, higher yields or commercial farm outcomes
rejected.reason: No such result is reported in the independently fetched full article.

rejected.claim: Autonomous pivot control or individual nozzle instructions
rejected.reason: The source supports a planned decision-support tool and controlled subsurface trial irrigation only.
Replace with a goal statement. The announcement contains no measured savings, but does not establish the current October trial status or prove that savings have never been tested elsewhere.
